verdict.rationale: turbopuffer's own docs list single-tenant and BYOC (bring-your-own-cloud) deployments alongside its default multi-tenant service, so the core product can run in a customer's own cloud environment. Nothing shows a downloadable, independently operable self-hosted distribution, and a community commenter notes it is source-unavailable. That is not a hands-on contradiction of BYOC, but it confirms there is no open-source self-host path. Missing for 10: documented self-managed install/operation of the core engine, details on what BYOC entails (who operates it, requirements), an on-prem or air-gapped option, independent corroboration of BYOC deployments.
